summary.name: Building good SLOs (CRE Life Lessons)
summary.one_liner: A Google Cloud Blog post by SRE Robert van Gent giving best practices for formulating service level objectives (SLOs) for service level indicators (SLIs), with worked availability and latency examples.
use_cases: Choosing SLO targets for a web service
Setting up error budgets and release policies
Deciding when to page on-call engineers
summary.what_it_does: Explains that SLOs are internal objectives distinct from SLAs and should cover the most critical user experience aspects. Recommends grouping queries by user experience, keeping SLOs simple, and not setting targets higher than needed. Gives availability SLO examples that count failures from the first controllable point, such as the load balancer, and latency SLOs expressed as the percentage of requests under a threshold rather than percentile values. Advises against average latency targets and against 100% targets, which leave no error budget. Recommends quarterly reporting, with shorter sliding windows for paging and release-freeze policies.
notable: Recommends expressing latency SLIs as percentage of requests under a threshold instead of p99 values
Advises against average (mean) latency targets because averages hide outliers
Recommends quarterly SLO reporting with shorter sliding windows for paging policies
Listed in the awesome-sre collection under Service Level Agreement
caveats: Describes Google's internal practices; examples are illustrative, not a product
Dated 2017 and assumes a Google-style SRE organization
